content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved their children to a new school just two days into the academic year.

According to Hello! magazine, which first reported the news, 5-year-old Prince Archie and 3-year-old Princess Lilibet were taken out of the school after concerns were raised by their security team.

Harry and Meghan's private security team reportedly pointed to potential risks faced by the family, including heavy traffic near the school and an extended commute. Hello! also reported that an incident had occurred which made it difficult for the family to travel together in a convoy.

A spokesperson for the Sussexes told HuffPost: "After consulting with their family security team and considering the practical challenges of the current arrangements, the decision was made to relocate the children."

The spokesperson added: "The parents are sincerely grateful to all the teachers and staff at the school for the care and thoughtful support they have provided to their family all along. This decision in no way reflects on the school or its outstanding care of their children."

Since stepping back from royal duties and losing the government-funded police protection, Harry has repeatedly expressed concerns about security arrangements when in the UK.

He has challenged the decision through the courts, arguing that the current arrangements leave him and his family exposed to significant risk.

Speaking to the BBC in May 2025 while his family was in the United States, Harry said: "I can't see myself being able to bring my wife and children back to the UK under the current circumstances."

The Daily Telegraph reported that, as they are currently in the UK, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) will conduct a fresh official risk assessment for the couple.
